title: Coordinate codimension in polynomial strict local rings
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $E$ a finite set, $P=k[T_i:i\in E]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $K\subseteq E$, and $\mathfrak q\subset P$ a prime ideal containing every $T_i$ for $i\in K$. Put $L=(T_i:i\in K)$, $Q=P/L\simeq k[T_j:j\in E\setminus K]$, and $\mathfrak q'=\mathfrak q/L\subset Q$. Use prime localizations as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Choose a separable closure of the residue field of $P_{\mathfrak q}$, which is canonically also the residue field of $Q_{\mathfrak q'}$. Let $R=(P_{\mathfrak q})^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $R'= (Q_{\mathfrak q'})^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be the strict henselizations relative to this choice [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. The four rings $P_{\mathfrak q}$, $Q_{\mathfrak q'}$, $R$, and $R'$ are Noetherian regular local rings [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Their Krull dimensions [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] satisfy
$$\dim P_{\mathfrak q}=\dim Q_{\mathfrak q'}+|K|,\qquad
\dim R=\dim P_{\mathfrak q},\qquad \dim R'=\dim Q_{\mathfrak q'},$$
and consequently $\dim R=\dim R'+|K|$. The assertion holds for arbitrary primes $\mathfrak q$, including nonmaximal ones, and includes $K=\varnothing$ and $K=E$.

source.place: Agent-supplied polynomial calculation realizing old step 8 and regularity in old step 7: Tag 00ON (lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total), Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space), Tag 00OQ (proposition-finite-gl-dim-polynomial-ring), Tag 06LN (lemma-henselization-regular), and Tag 06LK (lemma-henselization-dimension).

proof.text: Put $A=k[T_i:i\in K]$ and $\mathfrak m=(T_i:i\in K)\subset A$. Grouping monomials according to their exponents on $K$ and $E\setminus K$ gives $P\cong A[T_j:j\in E\setminus K]$. Evaluation at zero on the $K$-variables has kernel $L$: its kernel consists exactly of sums of monomials divisible by at least one such variable. Thus $Q\cong k[T_j:j\in E\setminus K]$. Similarly $A/\mathfrak m\cong k$, so $\mathfrak m$ is maximal; since $\mathfrak q\cap A$ is proper and contains $\mathfrak m$, it equals $\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space), origin specialization; the monomial calculation is written out here

proof.text: Apply polynomial regularity over the field $k$ to $A$, $P$, and $Q$ (choose finite enumerations of their variable sets). They are Noetherian, and their localizations at every prime are regular local. In particular $P_{\mathfrak q}$ and $Q_{\mathfrak q'}$ are Noetherian regular local rings. The origin-localization lemma applied to $A$ gives $\dim A_{\mathfrak m}=|K|$.

source.place: Tags 00OQ (proposition-finite-gl-dim-polynomial-ring), first sentence, and 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space), origin case

proof.text: View $A\to P$ as the coefficient inclusion into the polynomial ring on $E\setminus K$. The polynomial-projection lemma makes its affine spectrum map flat, and the affine flatness equivalence gives that $A\to P$ is a flat ring map. This is precisely the flatness needed in the height formula; no assumption that $\mathfrak q$ is maximal is made.

source.place: Tag 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize), coefficient inclusion into a polynomial algebra with its free monomial basis

proof.text: The local fibre in the height formula is $P_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak mP_{\mathfrak q}=P_{\mathfrak q}/LP_{\mathfrak q}\cong Q_{\mathfrak q'}$. Explicitly send the class of $f/s$ to $\bar f/\bar s$. A denominator $s\notin\mathfrak q$ has $\bar s\notin\mathfrak q'$, and every fraction on the right lifts this way. The inverse sends $\bar f/\bar s$ to the class of $f/s$; changing lifts changes numerator and denominator by elements of $L$, which vanish, and the fraction relation is preserved after multiplying by a denominator outside $\mathfrak q$. These maps are inverse. Quotienting further by the respective maximal ideals identifies the residue fields of $P_{\mathfrak q}$ and $Q_{\mathfrak q'}$.

source.place: Tag 00ON (lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total), local fibre term; fraction calculation for the coordinate quotient

proof.text: Apply the flat height formula to the Noetherian rings $A\to P$, the prime $\mathfrak q$, and its contraction $\mathfrak m$ from step 1. Its dimension form, the fibre isomorphism of step 4, and step 2 give $\dim P_{\mathfrak q}=\dim A_{\mathfrak m}+\dim Q_{\mathfrak q'}=|K|+\dim Q_{\mathfrak q'}$. Commuting the two summands gives the required first equality.

Both input local rings are Noetherian and regular by step 2. Strict-henselization regularity therefore makes $R$ and $R'$ regular local rings, hence Noetherian. Dimension invariance applied separately to the same two local rings gives $\dim R=\dim P_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\dim R'=\dim Q_{\mathfrak q'}$. Substitute these into step 5 to obtain $\dim R=\dim R'+|K|$. All applications allow the chosen separable closure of the common residue field. If $K=\varnothing$, $A=k$ and the added dimension is zero; if $K=E$, $Q=k$ and $\mathfrak q=L$. The same argument covers both.
